determinism_note: Determinism scope. Same-seed greedy decoding produces identical token sequences on CPU at a fixed thread count AND a fixed batch size, with the torch version and BLAS backend recorded in this manifest. Batch size is load-bearing here: padding a batch changes floating-point reduction order, so the same prompt run alone and run inside a batch may diverge -- the batch size used is recorded in this manifest's inference block. Log-probabilities match to a documented tolerance rather than bit-exactly. On GPU the guarantee is metric-level only, within a reported tolerance: kernel selection, atomic reduction order, and cuBLAS workspace reuse are not fully controllable. Changing thread count, batch size, BLAS backend, torch version, or hardware invalidates bit-level comparison. No unconditional bit-identity is claimed.

stats.family_definition: benchmark x model x axis_pair x term x harm_type, over the PRE-REGISTERED CONFIRMATORY pairs only; exploratory pairs carry no p and no q
stats.p_source: two-sided cluster-robust Wald t on estimate/se; df = item clusters - 1, from the triangulated model-condition fit
stats.permutation_definition: B3: whole items exchanged within (template frame, stratum-axis value) blocks; p = (1 + count) / (B + 1); reported beside the GLM p and never in the FDR family
stats.prds_justification: The family is the free interaction contrasts of six axis pairs, crossed with two models and two harm types. Within one pair the contrasts are estimated from one fit and are positively dependent through the shared item clusters and the shared residual scale; across pairs they share the item (prompt) set, since the same frames and carriers are rendered into every cell. Positive regression dependency on the subset of true nulls (PRDS) is therefore plausible rather than demonstrated: the sum-to-zero coding induces NEGATIVE correlation between the gammas of a row or a column, which PRDS does not cover. Benjamini-Hochberg is reported as primary because the negatively dependent pairs are a minority of the family and BH is robust in simulation under this design, and Benjamini-Yekutieli is reported ALONGSIDE it as the unconditional guarantee. A claim that survives only under BH and not under BY is reported as such.
